edit_summary: Replace each block's later Balance equalities by consecutive exact differences: for a block with existing indices k_1<...<k_m, emit B_1(x)=1 and B_j(x)-B_{j-1}(x)=0 (j=2..m), RHS 1 -> 0 for the 1046 differenced rows. The transformation matrix per block is unit lower bidiagonal (prefix-sum inverse), so the feasible set is preserved exactly in both the integer and the LP domain; 1096 forward and 1096 cumulative-inverse identities were checked by the agent.
claims: 4 claims = (integer, LP domain) x (forward, reverse); objective 'Equal' in all four; projection is the identity on all 16,392 coordinates in every claim; hand-written inverse pairing [1,0,3,2] (cases/test68/request.json).
Obligations per claim 70481 / 70481 / 69089 / 69089 = 279,140 total; 1,046 linear steps per claim (cases/test68/preparation.json).
Forward: each differenced target row is a Lin Eq fact new[k] = old[k] - old[k-1]; the first row of each of the 50 blocks stays a direct RowEq ref (cases/test68/README.md).
Reverse: old[k] = new[k] + old[k-1] reuses the predecessor's Local ref, keeping the inverse linear in block length (cases/test68/README.md; tools/prepare_affine.py:112).
Every coordinate's bounds and integrality, the identity projection and the full affine inverse identities are discharged per claim as 'Exact' entries (tools/prepare_affine.py:146-147).

Steps: 4 x 1,046 Lin facts, kind 'Eq', constant 0, two terms each, e.g. [[{'RowEq':1},'1'],[{'RowEq':0},'-1']] (~101 KB per block).
Return maps are the identity written out in full: 4 x 628,179 B = 2,512,716 B, each 16,392 single-term Exprs.
checks total 3,709,732 B: VarLower 1,201,352 B, VarUpper 1,201,352 B, 'Exact' 1,071,392 B (identity projections, inverses, integrality), 3,520 row refs 235,636 B.
Identity/per-coordinate scaffolding = 6,794,023 B of 7,455,486 B (91%); the 1,046-row difference rule itself is 403,302 B (5.4%).

agent_manual_work: Parsed all 194,732 lines of the 11,539,189 B MPS exactly with Fraction (one Decimal cross-read) and checked every row sense, coefficient, RHS, bound, integer marker and section header (digest evals 'Mapping MPS sections', 'Parsing exact model representation').

Exhaustively confirmed sum_{s<=k<=t} X_i_s_t = 1 for all 1,096 Balance rows, then formed the differences and inverted them: 1,096 forward and 1,096 cumulative identities (digest eval 'Verifying sparse equality transformation').

Wrote the 5,748,109 B reformulated MPS record-by-record, preserving every untouched column, RHS and marker line and asserting emitted_balance == set(new_col_bal) (digest eval 'Writing committed sparse formulation').

Invented the audit schema itself: output/audit.json (333,527 B) lists per-row source rows with multipliers, original/new RHS, unchanged scope and file hashes instead of dumping coefficients (digest report section 6).
Wrote output/verify.py (8,136 B), an independent second reader using extended fixed-field positions and Decimal->Fraction, which re-checked both files and returned PASS.
friction: Target construction is external to the kernel: the 1,046-row difference target is the agent's own MPS writer output; the certificate keeps only the finished target.mcm and never carries the edit.

No typed edit schema: request.json carries only reverse / input_integers / output_integers / objective / projection / inverse, so the edit binding is an untrusted audit.json joined by row-name strings with hand-written asserts (prepare_affine.py:107-112).

Duplicated scaffolding: the same 16,392-pair identity projection is written 4x inside proof.rpa (829,515 B) and a 5th time as request.json (829,516 B); each identity Return map (628,179 B) is written 4x.

Resource surprise: the identical RPA and request returned RESOURCE_LIMIT exit 3 ('proof work budget') under kernel cc96f69d..., then VERIFIED under kernel c699e384... at work 4,433,660 - artifact size does not predict the cost.
Two competing claim builders coexist: prepare_test40.py:104 build_claim (not used here) and prepare_affine.py:122 block, each with its own MPS parse (prepare_test40.py:20 vs prepare_affine.py:20).
shape_preserving_pair: Batch pair test67 + test68 are both same-coordinate shape-preserving certified rewrites (36864/33791 and 16392/3520 unchanged) generated from this library with identity Return maps (measured: test67 2 claims x 36,864 coords, checks 218,113/218,112, claims bytes 988,000; test68 4 claims x 16,392 coords, checks 70,481/70,481/69,089/69,089). They need the same core capabilities: compact identity map/projection and per-coordinate obligation families, a kernel-side edit audit, and typed rule builders. test67 additionally needs bounded local refutations, Cases/propagation, a feasible point witness and an objective lower bound (cases/test67/preparation.json), which test68 does not.
edit_representability: Coefficient-level edits are provable in the proof layer but not declarable in the claim/audit layer. Kernel Lin facts accept arbitrary rational multipliers over any Ref, which is exactly how the 1,046 difference rows are proved (proof.rpa steps [[RowEq:k,1],[RowEq:k-1,-1]]; prepare_affine.py:133-143), but the claim layer exposes only reverse, input/output integer modes, objective relation, projection and inverse (docs/CURRENT_FORMAT.md:98-105,338-341) - no per-row, per-coefficient or per-edit record - so the edit list stays outside the certificate as audit.json. Kind-level edits are absent from this case (report section 4: all row names and senses unchanged) and are equally undeclared: the preparer copies the Lin kind from the target row's sense ('Eq' vs 'Le', prepare_affine.py:131,141) and only the claim's integer-mode flags can hint at a domain change.

library_subsumption: Mcm::load plus typed row/var access removes parse_mps (45 lines) and row_ref and retires the toolchain's third MPS parser (prepare_affine.py:20, prepare_test40.py:20).
A typed edit-audit record plus rule builders replace derivation()/block() per-case branches; the affine family (test21/23/33/37/40/44/48/65/68/77/78/79/88) reduces to one plan call per case.
Span/template encoding of homogeneous obligations removes the mapping/checks/projection loops and lets claim planning report obligation counts per claim before assembly.
Plan preflight removes the assemble-verify-rerun cycle that the resource baseline records for this case.
